title: Instrumenting the application: metrics, logs and traces

videos.script: Until now, every measurement of the box office came from outside it. In production nobody is watching when the load arrives. {{outside}} So the box office learns to report on itself. A counter for every request, a histogram for how long each took, and a line of log for each one. {{instrument}} Prometheus asks each copy for its numbers every five seconds. {{scrape}} Under load, the box office says four hundred and seventy nine reads and three hundred and thirty eight sales a second. The load generator, measuring from outside, agrees. {{rates}} A histogram keeps counts in buckets, so its percentile is an estimate, and you will see exactly how wide. {{buckets}} Then a replica crashes, and the same failure shows up as an error for the client, a line in the log and a count in the metrics. {{error}} Last, the one label that would turn sixty six series into six million, and an objective the box office can be held to. {{slo}}
